review_text_raw:
Overall, I do like the concept behind Simulacra, it gave me a lot of flashbacks to a game called Orwell which also had a very voyeristic/technological vibe and left me wanting to explore more and learn more about the people I was encountering.

However, I have one single criticism of this game based on my experience so far that I think has somewhat soured my opinion of what otherwise seems to be a great horror title with a novel concept, that being the jump scares.

They're completely unessercary and feel rather out of place, the situation the game presents you with is already creepy and uncomfortable enough on it's own without needing to throw up distorted pictures with loud bursts of white noise, it didn't draw me deeper into the experience, it actually yanked me firmly out of it and discouraged me from further exploring the various areas of the phone and probing for more details and information (seeing as I'm not particularly fond of jump scares and random exploration seems like a good way to stumble upon them).

I'd say if someone was going to make another game in this style, have confidence that your concept is creepy enough to draw people in, it'd make a nice change to see more horror titles content to let their horror have a slow, deep burn rather than a quick, short lived flash.

review_text_raw:
A supernatural horror story where you use a missing person's phone (texting contacts/viewing photos/reading e-mail/other apps or social media) to figure out what happened to them. Not the same but it gives a similar feel to me as a game like Orwell.

I don't really enjoy horror games in general so I preferred playing this game as a mystery. I didn't really care for the random 'horror' sound effects or imagery. I was a bit disappointed when the plot went for [spoiler]the sci-fi twist. It's alright but I would have liked a regular, more realistic thing. It felt like something outside of your control with no real foreshadowing or buildup. There is nothing to suggest that it was possible and even after you learn about it you can't go back and see much in a new light. It might be nice if they at least put something random about the dangers of AI or something.[/spoiler]

Aside from the general phone-searching there are some minigames. They aren't too tough but one might be harder if you're not a native english speaker. One minigame is taking a jumbled list of words and making the right sentence out of it. However, it's not enough to get an equivalent meaning- you have to get the word order exactly right. For example, 'Meet me and I'll show ya this weekend' is wrong but 'Meet me this weekend and I'll show ya' is right.

Worth a look if you're fine with learning about the missing person story through phone history and dialogue.

Other thoughts:[list]
[*] It's a little annoying that in order to get the 'good' ending you have to [spoiler]manipulate people because there's no way to convince them otherwise.[/spoiler]
[*] I would have liked multiple save slots.
[*] It's nice that it can be set to automatically skip text on repeat playthroughs.
[*] Pretty much no settings to adjust (only subtitles). I would've liked at least volume and resolution options.
[*] Some inconsistencies/strange things: [spoiler]She met Taylor on Spark but had been following him on Jabbr 3 months ago. Cassie's AMA from 3 months ago is still continuing even though it closed (you get to ask a question)? The article mentions a back-and-forth between genders but you're forced to repeat the female gender and use one of the three pre-selected photos (it seems like other pictures don't progress the story). Why is it assimilating the 'weak'? From what I understand it's somehow taking control of a person and building a world out of their simulacrum (online personification?)? And then discarding the physical body for some reason because they can only lure in one person on Spark before they're useless?[/spoiler]
[*] A bunch of grammar and spelling errors and incorrect subtitles.
[*] Only crashed randomly once.
[/list]

review_text_raw:
I'm going to divide this review into various sections based on gameplay elements, in a slightly illogical order. This seems appropriate for a slightly illogical game. Also, I ran out of characters, so I had to leave a lot out.

[h2] Sound Design [/h2]
Best part of the game. Only thing that makes it scary.

Even for someone who had quite a few scares spoiled for me due to watching previous playthrough snippits and common internet knowledge, the scares still all GOT ME. And, I mean, they GOT ME. I was jumping in my seat and looking around for the voices I was hearing. At one point [spoiler] I heard a door knocking and thought someone was trying to break into my bedroom [/spoiler]. Those sounds that play, whether phone ringing or human breathing or that terrible [spoiler] wood knocking [/spoiler], were still enough to make me jump after four straight playthroughs. Every time, I'd finish, and I'd think, this is no Doki Doki Literature Club, I can get through this without jumping. But then there'd be a cellphone ringing or glitched sound or Anna breathing at me and, however slight, I'd jump. The sound in this game was so effective it almost wasn't fair. 

That said, the only thing that was what I can only accurately describe as mid was the voice for the [spoiler] Simulacra [/spoiler]. I'll go into this later, but I got to the end of the game so freaked out by the sound at the beginning, that this didn't leave much an impact.

[h2] Music [/h2]
There isn't as much to gush about here. I'd say it does its job and the title screen is iconic.Part of me wishes I had some more songs to add to my gamer Main Character Syndrome Spotify playlist, but I also do think limiting the soundtrack and sticking to eiry silence cut off by that terrifying sound design is the way to go.

[h2] Characters [/h2]
If I ever found a missing person's phone, and everyone treated me like this, I'd either 1. Say she's better off missing or 2. Just hand the phone off to the cops. 

[h3] Anna [/h3]
They really try to make her sympathetic. She's rejected from vet school and she's just gotten out of a toxic relationship, her workplace is awful and she's being harrassed by her boss and coworker. Now, with all that laid out, you might be wondering, what don't you like about her? She's clearly very layered and passionate and look at all the bad stuff happening to her. She's so sympathetic!

Yes, there are lots of bad things happening to her. But other than the fact that she likes animals and is really bad at picking people to be around, I can't tell you one thing about her. She's just very bland. Honestly, I wonder if it would be more interesting if it was Greg we were supposed to find. Be told by everyone how important it is to hunt him down and bring him back, slowly uncovering that he's not that great of a person, having to contemplate with the consequences of what it would mean to actually bring the jerk back. Anna being the one we need to bring back is just kind of...eh? These people really want her back in their lives and whole time I was just wondering, why? She's cardboard. 

[h3] Taylor [/h3]
He tells bad jokes but you can tell deep down he's got a big heart. He's made some big mistakes and honestly comes off as a bit of a creep. I wasn't sure what exactly he liked about Anna, but that's beside the point. Actually, yeah, that is my only gripe with him. Why is he so invested in the life of a chick he's talked to on a dating app one time? I mean this man goes to her and begs for her and puts himself in danger for her. That's a lot of work for cardboard you saw on sale on Ebay. 

[h3] Greg [/h3]
People like to rip on the actor for this guy, and yeah, I get it. I'm not sure if I was supposed to be laughing at him or if he was supposed to tick me off or if heaven forbid he was supposed to scare me, but he did two of three (i'm sure you can guess which ones). I think Greg sees Anna as someone who he can easily control and manipulate. Which makes sense. She is cardboard. I did find it odd on one route where he [spoiler] suddenly abandons pursuing Anna as soon as he learns the cops are after him [/spoiler]. It came out of left field and then you never learn what happens to him from that point. Honestly, I love to hate Greg, so I think he does his job. I can understand him being obsessive over Anna since 1. they dated for two years and 2. she sees her as easy. 

[h3] Ashley [/h3]
THIS GIRL TICKED ME OFF. I'm not talking about the route where you [spoiler] lie to her and manipulate her into saying she's in love with Anna, though again I ask WHY [/spoiler]. I'm talking about how she treats you if you come clean right away and just tell her who you are and why you have Anna's phone. She flips, gets super defensive. won't let you explain yourself, and then calls the cops on you. She'll randomly disappear from the plot and go offline, and she won't work with you no matter what you say to her. I find that highly improbable. I don't think they knew what to do with Ashley for the routes where [spoiler] she knows the truth [/spoiler].

[h3] Everyone else [/h3]
Nothing much to report. No one made me as mad as Anna's supposed BFF. So good job.

[h3] Simulacra [/h3]
Alright, I have an issue. This thing isn't scary. There's so much buildup, then it's just kind of there. It's so melodramatic and easy to make fun of. I almost think this story would've been better of Greg had just killed her or something. I don't understand how this thing kills or kidnaps, I'm not scared of it, and it keeps changing the rules. I dunno, I just wanted one last big scare, or something that felt satisfying after all that buildup. Then I saw it, and I thought, that's it?

[h2] Story [/h2]
In this game you find a phone that is clearly possessed, and are tasked to find its owner, Anna. You are helped and hindered by the various people trying to get ahold of her, and you can either leave her life in shambles for her to return to or make her life better with your interference. 

Some aspects were rewarding. I liked getting to put that one workplace creep in his place. I liked when I got her a new job in that one playthrough.

I think the main issues with the story were already discussed in the characters section. I don't think the payoff was satisfying. I think I see what they are going for, with the good ending that is. You have to become a master manipulator to take down the manipulator, I do like that. Again, I just felt like the final boss was an absolute joke. I thought it was fake, there was another boss behind the boss, or something. I think the plot excels in relationship drama and just making terrible people act terrible. It's guilty pleasure level entertaining. It gets lost in the big ideas and trying to be bigger than it actually is. I think if it had stuck to a nitty gritty found phone horror game, with people as its worst enemy, it would've stuck the landing a bit more.

[h2] Theme [/h2]
Dating apps bad. Something about valuing the real world over the virtual. Game certainly doesn't punish you much for becoming a master online troll catfishing manipulator. But maybe...maybe that's the real point. We can look back at a preinternet time and recognize that certain things were better back then. But the fact of the matter is, that world doesn't exist anymore. 

Wow. That went deeper than I thought. Too bad the villian sucks and I don't care about Anna. 

[h1] Wait, didn't you recommend this game? I'm confused [/h1]
Yes. I do.

I think it's fun. Fun like watching the Scream franchise. Fun like a haunted hayride sponsored by a high school, where you know things are corny, but you know what, for those couple of times they made you jump, it was worth spending a couple bucks for a ride. Just wait for a Steam sale and get it for like a dollar like I did. This was a really well spent dollar.

review_text_raw:
☑ Great story
☑ Unique setting and storytelling
☑ Horror vibes on point
☑ Multiple endings and various easter eggs
☑ "Begin+" mode that allows you to fast-forward through conversations after you clear the game once
☑ Creepy OS stalks you and provides helpful notes and to-do list
☑ Occasional random creepy sound effects on stereo that don't sound like they're from the game so they always freak you out
☑ Ability to freely change Anna's dating profile, comment on her social media, etc.
☑ Creepy OS will scold you if you use "foul language"

A banger. Loved it.

One criticism, devs: get a native English speaker to proofread things. Simulacra can get away with poor English better than most games because you can just pass mistakes off as typos, but at a certain point it just becomes clear that the script was written by non-native speakers.

review_text_raw:
When you are a mature person and your childhood and carefree days are already over, you have kinda stressful job, you don't feel like playing hard games, or games where you have to concentrate a lot. Sometimes, you just want to come over to your place. make yourself a cup of tea and just relax on comfortable chair and just enjoy some kinda easy game. Preferably, with a mouse only controls.

But to be honest, you need to be ready that games will be strange, or better call them weird or maybe even creepy in some kinda way, cause variety of the titles, that can be played with mouse only is pretty limited and you should expect only chinese visual novels, or some nonsense clickers, or easy tower defense games, or some puzzle logic games.

Or it can be a game like Simulacra. I am not even sure how to call this genre, but what I really do know for sure - this game is completely stupid :) But, in a good funny way. They call it a simulation game, which is kinda fair, but doesn't cover the whole idea of this game. 

So, you start the game playing as not a man, not a woman, just whoever the hell you are, sex is not specified in this game. You found a smartphone and this is where the whole stupid part is about to start. I mean like, imagine you are that person who found a phone, okay? What you gonna do? For me it's completely obvious and easy - if phone is unlockable, you simply need to find someone with a name Mom, Dad, Sister, Boyfriend, Dog in a contact list, call one of them and let them know that you found this device and return it as soon as possible. In case phone is locked, you just need to go to the police station and give it to them for the further actions. Easy as that, don't you think so? But not for our protagonist! Instead all of this, he/she decides to play around with this phone and read messages/mail, check web history, tinder-alike app - I mean like literally everything what you don't have to do, when you find someone's phone, cause this is simply embarassing. For the whole game I had that feeling that I was playing as a retard, who had no job, no personal life, no entertainment sources, literally nothing, so that phone was a greatest relief ever. 

But, on the other hand, if that person wouldn't be that miserable and pathetic and wouldn't check that messages and videos on the camera roll - he wouldn't realize that phones belonged to someone who was desperately crying for help, stucked in some kinda danger. The more you click on that stupid phone the more stranger and uglier everything becomes, and you have to solve some kinda puzzles. All these puzzle things are more like "choose the right answer" in dialogues with a random people, talking about phone's owner, which is also a random person for you lol, which you shouldn't care about at all and all these combinations of answers lead you to different endings. Plus you have to recreate some corrupted messages, by putting words in the right order and renew corrupted photos by clicking on image pieces at the right order. Time to time, you will see ugly screamers on the phone, whose aim is to scarry you and like, to be honest, this one of the most ridiculous things in this game, cause I was laughing all the time when that was appearing on the screen, so I can't say that this game is a horror experience, it's more "wannabe horror game" , trying to be mysterious and creepy all the way ends up with a pretty shallow and a bit boring idea.

However, I can recommend this game. It brings you some fresh new experience and can be funny a little bit plus you can relax after a busy stressful day by just clicking on the dialogue options and solving pretty easy puzzles trying to figure out what the hell is going on there. 

So, to sum everything up!
You should grab this game if you: 

+ Feel like playing some easy game, where is no need for high concentration
+ Are a Black Mirror TV show fan and like all this paranoic idea about how it can be bad somewhere in the future for us with all these high-tech devices
+ Don't agree with me, that carrying a phone to the police station would be the best idea in this situation :)
+ Just looking for a new experience

Avoid this game if you:

- Don't like illogical games, with a stupid protagonist who has no idea what the hell is he doing 
- Have no desire to try something new and unusual

Enjoy!

Time to time, you will see ugly screamers on the phone, whose aim is to scarry you and like, to be honest, this one of the most ridiculous things in this game, cause I was laughing all the time when that was appearing on the screen, so I can't say that this game is a horror experience, it's more "wannabe horror game" , trying to be mysterious and creepy all the way ends up with a pretty shallow and a bit boring idea. However, I can recommend this game. It brings you some fresh new experience and can be funny a little bit plus you can relax after a busy stressful day by just clicking on the dialogue options and solving pretty easy puzzles trying to figure out what the hell is going on there. So, to sum everything up! You should grab this game if you: + Feel like playing some easy game, where is no need for high concentration + Are a Black Mirror TV show fan and like all this paranoic idea about how it can be bad somewhere in the future for us with all these high-tech devices + Don't agree with me, that carrying a phone to the police station would be the best idea in this situation :) + Just looking for a new experience Avoid this game if you: - Don't like illogical games, with a stupid protagonist who has no idea what the hell is he doing - Have no desire to try something new and unusual Enjoy!

tl;dr if you want a phone snooping game that is better than this (harder puzzles, better writing) + touches on some of the same themes, and don't mind it being non-horror, try out [b]Another Lost Phone: Laura's Story[/b].

I really like the conceit of a fake computer or phone as the setting for a mystery game, which is why a friend recommended I play this. However, I can't say that I would do the same.

The writing is riddled with typos and unnatural grammatical errors. Like, a lot of these characters aren't even convincingly fluent English speakers. (Also the way their only Black character is written is. reductive.) But it does have its moments that feel natural and compelling.

The acting is... bad. They sound like they're reading off a teleprompter one word at a time, rather than speaking a sentence, and the emotional reactions are not convincing. Worst of the bunch is, unfortunately, one of the two guys whose voice you hear the most. [spoiler](By which I mean Greg.)[/spoiler]

The characterization is weird? IDK, you spend most of your time talking to various brands of Men Who Are Creepy To Women, and it keeps asking you to side with at least one of them. [spoiler]By the way, one of them is a registered sex offender. And somehow, that's not even the reason he's creepy![/spoiler] Even your interactions with the women in the cast are usually about various aforementioned creepy men. [spoiler]The closeted lesbian coming out to (she believes) the woman she has a crush on? That conversation fails the Bechdel test, even if you consider the player impersonating Anna to be a "named woman."[/spoiler] So even though it's supposed to be about Anna, it's more accurately about men fighting over a woman-shaped trophy called Anna.
It may seem like I'm kind of harping on this but that's only because so MUCH of their characterization is either behaving inappropriately towards women or being belligerent to people in general. There's not much to go on without that.

As for the narrative, it was... railroady. I didn't feel like I was finding secrets because even if I found out something a little early, one of the guys would just tell me to do it later. The highly telegraphed railroading in the intro was actually my favorite UI moment in the game, but that was a lot more artful than the clumsy dialogue trees that all lead to a single point.
I did think the big bad was interesting, especially the part about [spoiler]how "a strong individual would simulate a better [life]" rather than live fully in a suboptimal one[/spoiler]. Though I felt like that theme of [spoiler]the appearance being more meaningful than the substance[/spoiler], while present in some parts of the game, such as [spoiler]reporting a colleague for harassment being an issue because it could reflect poorly on the company, or the folder of pictures of random women that Taylor just Has, Apparently[/spoiler], was underutilized. Which is odd, because... that's from your villain monologue—you HAVE to establish those themes in the story up to that point.

There's just a lot that could have been considerably better than it was.

[b]Last time I pick up a random phone.[/b]

One day, you find a phone just sitting on your doorstep. Like anybody else, you decide to snoop through the phone either to figure out who the owner is so you can return it or just because you can. However, this turns into a much more complicated situation. The first tip off is that while you are blocked by a lock screen, the phone glitches so you can get into it. I don’t know about anybody else, but I wouldn’t have looked through it after that. Anyway, you soon find out that the phone’s owner is Anna and she has recently gone missing. Thus, you decide to look through her phone activity and talk to her friends and acquaintances in an attempt to find her before it’s too late.

There are some puzzles here with the most frequent puzzle you’ll come across involves unscrambling text messages and photos. For texts, you’ll have to order the words in the right order. Photos are more complicated as you’re given several fragments to piece together, but you can’t have any part that is glitched. So you’ll have to figure out which order will allow all glitched out parts to be replaced with the picture. The other puzzle you’ll come across involve you gathering information through either the sites Anna frequented or through her friends. The only problem I had was that some messages had more than one way that it could make sense and that there is an instance where you’re expected to remember certain facts since you can’t go and look for the information.

The acting is average, with Anna’s actress being the stand out, with hilariously bad parts (aka all of Greg’s voice lines) sprinkled in. Voice acting mainly comes through Anna’s vlogs, audio text messages, and phone calls. What doesn’t exactly make sense are the phone calls. At certain points in the story, you’ll get a phone call from one of the characters and you’ll have to answer it (or they’ll keep calling/story won’t continue). Of course, you can’t answer back and when that character asks why you don’t talk back, the excuse is that you can’t make out what they’re saying (despite you being able to hear them fine). I’d rather have the excuse either be that you guess the mic got broken before you found it (which can also imply that whatever is making the phone glitch is causing the mic to stop working) or it auto sends them to voicemail. [spoiler]It doesn’t make sense even more when a police officer actually calls you but assume he’s leaving a voicemail despite not hearing “leave a message after the beep”.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]Also, I just couldn’t help but laugh at the look she gives Taylor in the ending where both of them live.[/spoiler]

Simulacra has four endings each with their own requirements. While you can’t jump to a specific section of the game, you’ll be able to speed things up on your next playthroughs through Begin+. It won’t take long to build up the requirements you need, but the last sequence plays at the same speed.

While Simulacra isn’t perfect, it’s still worth it to experience it yourself, whether it be on PC or on your phone to get the maximum immersion you can. I did find the phone aspect convincing for the most part, didn’t mind that glitches were used to freak you out (though others might not like it), and liked how they filled in the empty space with a room with ambient noises chiming in. There are even some subtle moments here, like the phone’s background changing. The only thing that really messes with immersion is some of the voice acting.

TL;DR: Posting this review to help Steam out, since this game does NOT deserve such praise. Honestly, I would have been annoyed but said screw it if it was at "Very Positive"... but overwhelmingly positive? It literally does nothing new, innovative, or even good. In fact, I'd say the only thing it accomplished was copying things done many times before it in an absolutely terrible way. It was a slog to get through from beginning to end. I can honestly say it combined all the crappiest parts of horror movie trailers, the worst creepypastas and a s****y jigsaw puzzle together in a terrible phone-shaped package that lasted for WAY too long. It was 30 minutes of terrible content somehow stretched into 3 hours. In other words, if you get it in a bundle like me, go ahead and stop playing when you decide the moment is right. It's not going to get better.

Got this from the "Overwhelmingly Positive" Humble Bundle. How in the actual f*** is this game "Overwhelmingly Positive" ????? Kids review bomb awesome games on here all the time, and this managed to survive that for so long? I'm legitimately confused and concerned. Did this game get massive press in some media targeted specifically towards children, and somehow avoid literally everyone else? Did the people who hate it just not care enough to leave a review? Again, were on Steam, so how?????

On a particularly boring night, I played the entire damn thing. The first 5 minutes in I already knew it was going to be terrible, but stupidly I played on, hoping for something redeeming to happen to justify the positive reviews and my time wasted. That obviously didn't happen.

Bad writing, bad puzzles, atrocious "scares" (literally all jumps, flashing images and noises, and even then not a single f***ing one even managed a startled shutter from me, with volume annoyingly high), all set to an all-too-overplayed by now "hey, play this game on this device/OS/form of communication" gimmick that I'm frankly by now beyond tired of game developers using as a replacement for an interesting story/plot/writing (Stories Untold is the most recent game to do it RIGHT AFAIK). It was cool like the first 100 times maybe, but I'm over it.

I also want to point out, I don't think I have EVER seen good writing/plot in a game that has characters communicating through a messaging system, then has every character using terrible grammar, punctuation, etc. It bugs the hell out of me.
1.It's usually inconsistent. Some chatacters just spring in and out of it randomly.
2.We're not all 12. Some people actually care about that kind of stuff, so it doesn't make sense to have EVERYONE at some point talking like the slow, overly emotional kid in class.
3.It isn't 1995 anymore. It's one thing to have every character talk like that when they're using AOL Instant Messenger, but for chrissakes, you actually have to make an EFFORT to screw up grammar the way these characters do on a modern cellphone with autocorrect. Ugh.

review_text_raw:
OK, I have just finished one run and I would recommend it!
In shorts,

Goods:
+Lots of contents, even some random guys on Spark, very detailed characterized even for minor characters
+Climax just bumped into at the right moments
+Innovative gameplay rather than just points and clicks
+Real action characters make the game much more immersive
+There are just right amount of minigames beside pure text reading
+Spot on the mentality that people like to check on others' phones and see what're inside, eg. Gallery, videos, etc
+Low price tag!

Bads:
-I can't say Anna is poor at acting, she's good, but she's kind of zoned out during the first second of most of the clips. It looks like that she is thinking what to say then starts acting after one second
-Some unnecessary jumpscares, the script is good, the story is good, come on, you can make the atmosphere scary without cheap jumpscares, make it more subtle, eg. Anna's wallpaper is changing after certain stages, which is spooky and good
-The ending is not so good... The whole process is great but when it comes to the ending... I am ok with the setting but it would be great if the ending part was made longer
-So during the ending part, Taylor is still busy texting you when he's encountering all those shxx? That doesn't make any sense. I understand that there has to be a means to let the players know what is happening. Can't you just make it like Taylor used Facetime with you before all those happened and try to tell the story with videos? As I imagine the scene, I found it very weird that Taylor is dealing with those things and keeps looking at the phone and texts you back and forth. That would be a heavy smartphone addict...
-The story is too long but very linear, which makes replays not quite possible. I want to try the other endings, but it's harsh for me to go for another 4-hour KNOWN adventure. There are many side events to do but the main route is pretty much the same. Maybe you can make it that we start at some certain late points or make the story less linear. We don't like grinding...

That being said, it's still a very great game, I hope there are more localization subtitles coming soon that I can refer to more of my friends from other parts of the world.
I will def buy the next title from Kaigon Games!
Good job! :p

I really love this game genre, but this specific game wasn't very good in my opinion, for the following reasons:
- Inconsistent plot. The game just makes use of random horror movie tropes, without them making sense in the story.
- Very cringey characters (both due to the bad writing and to the bad acting), ESPECIALLY the two most important characters in the game: the girl you're supposed to find and the ultimate bad guy. That's a real problem, because it makes it very hard to emphatize with the person you're supposed to save, as well as to take the bad guy seriously.
- Random jumpscares make this game feel pretty shallow.
- Very, very often, the choices that are proposed to you seem forced. Basically, you can feel that the game WANTS the story to progress in a specific direction, and doesn't allow you to very simply avoid issues by being reasonable. For example, at some point, you can either tell a very dangerous lie or tell the truth. But if you tell the truth, at no point does the game allow to explain yourself, and therefore the person you told the truth to just reacts badly for no reason. In real life it would have been easy to avoid that issue, but the game doesn't want that. Hence, choices aren't well made, and overall it doesn't feel like you're really making story progress - it actually more feels like you're following the story where it wants you to go.

Still, there also are some good things:
- The phone interface looks pretty realistic, which is at least one immersive thing
- One playthrough is reasonably long (about 4 hours for the first one), especially since the game is very cheap, and there apparently are four different endings. 
- One or two moments in the story were actually pretty interesting, even though they didn't make sense in the grand scheme of things

Overall, I advice against buying this game, as there are many better ones in the same genre; I for example enjoyed Orwell much more, and both its mechanics and thematics are somewhat similar (without the horror movie aspect of it, which is good riddance honestly), but the writing is much better and realistic (and therefore more immersive as well !) and never made me cringe. Still, Simulacra is very cheap, so if you're okay with what I said above, go ahead.

review_text_raw:
Now this is how you do a smartphone mystery right. The concept of Sara is Missing was sound, but the execution was poor. However, Kaigan Games took the concept and criticism, and further developed the core concept further in Simulacra. 

Simulacra does a fantastic job in making you the player feel lost and isolated. You are in a dimly lit room with constant noises around you - you are never allowed to feel comfortable where you are, or with what you are doing. You have a random woman's phone, and it is up to you to find her. You have to dig through her e-mails, Jabber and Spark accounts, and decide which of her friends and acquaintances can be trusted with crucial information related to Anna's disappearance.

The tension is real. Should you really be doing this? Wouldn't it be easier to just contact the police? But can the police even find her with so little information? Which of her friends can be trusted? Could one of them be responsible for her disappearance?  The whole time something feels off from the very beginning. Are you being watched? 

The only real gripe I have with the game is the jump scares. Jump scares are for cheap low-level horror titles. And I don't necessarily mean cheap in terms of dollar value - a lot of AAA titles misuse jump scares and it's pathetic. One or two carefully placed jump scares in appropriate games is fine, but Simulacra isn't one of them. The fear comes from the tension and subtle little nuances. When the phone goes crazy and suddenly the picture of Anna on the wallpaper changes slightly, but you're not sure if you imagined it or not - perfect. Loud noises and jumbled up pictures - stupid. 

All-in-all Simulacra is a terrific experience if you like these kind of horror games. Don't let Sara is Missing deter you from trying out Kaigan Games other titles, unlike a lot of other developers, they took the criticisms they received and learned from them to craft better experiences. That alone makes this game worth checking out.

review_text_raw:
The Good Stuff:

The layout and idea behind the game is pretty cool. I like how each "app" generally feels like a real app where you can do whatever, like comment of peoples posts or call random numbers. It is really neat design idea and it is well executed.

I also enjoyed a few of the more difficult puzzles, as they really added a sense of immersion into digging through someone's phone. The puzzles are mainly pretty easy, but the game doesn't baby you through them at all, so you feel smart when you manage to pull of something a bit more complicated.

The Bad Stuff:

For me, story is one of the most important parts of a game like this, and unfortunately SIMULACRA fails to deliver a good one.

Mild Spoilers: [spoiler]While the ending tried to be Black Mirror-esque, I feel like the story fails to properly set up the ending, so it kinda comes out of nowhere. Also, many things in the story aren't well explained or left to Deus Ex Machina[/spoiler]

There are multiple endings, and you will get an idea of what they all are when you finish the game. Some of the potential outcomes have me slightly curious, but not enough to replay it to see them. Perhaps the story would have been more interesting had I gotten a different ending.

I am not a huge fan of horror, but I have played games like Prey and Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice that have a creepy horror feel. The creepiness of SIMULACRA lasts only about the first 30 mins and then you become generally innoculated.

The main title song was also pretty cheesy.

As many other reviews have pointed out, some of the voice acting is on the level of "so bad it's hilarious".

I understand that with a smaller scale game like this it is difficult, but I felt like the chat options often strong-armed me into things I didn't want to say, which made things like [spoiler]gaining Taylor's trust[/spoiler] feel unfair.

The Bottom Line: If you want a game with a good story, there are better games. If you want a game where choices matter, there are better games. If you want a horror game, there are better games. If you just want to see a cool mechanic in action, then you might want to check it out.

review_text_raw:
In Simulacra you find yourself in possession of a stranger's (Anna) phone, who seems to have come to some harm. Through interactions with her phone via video logs, old chat messages, pictures, etc, you gain access to Anna's backstory. Going forward, primarily through "live" chats with Anna's acquaintances, and interactions with some of the other apps on the phone, you unravel the story.

Pros:
[list]
[*] The story progression as implemented through the interactions with the phone apps is OK.
[*] The real-life acting done by Anna and Taylor was good.
[*] The concept of this experience was novel (at least to me).
[/list]

YMMV:
[list]
[*] There are different endings possible, as a function of your choices. I typically don't like this choose-your-adventure type of feature, as it turns into a "guess what the dev" wants me to say sort of thing. Also, this game is nowhere near interesting enough to warrant a second play through, so you are stuck with whatever ending your seemingly random choices yield. For me, this was the "bad" (maybe even super bad?) ending, which left a bad taste in my mouth, and made me feel as though I had wasted my time.
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*] The two oft repeated mini-games aren't really fun, and seem shoe-horned in, in an effort to somehow make this more into a game. It doesn't really work. I would classify this as an "experience" more than a "game".
[*] The story itself was underwhelming. 
[/list]

Conclusion: Read the reviews carefully before purchasing this one and get it on sale. It may be a mildly amusing way to pass several hours, but it certainly isn't for everyone. Giving a weak-thumbs up due to binary rating system.

Overall: 5.0/10

review_text_raw:
I enjoy these 'immersive sim' games where you look through devices for clues to a mystery like A Normal Lost Phone or even Hypnospace Outlaw. I liked trawling through old messages and finding tidbits of information that would help me solve a mystery or hack into a passworded account to find more clues. 

I thought that Simulacra would be similar to those kinds of games, but maybe with a more harrowing twist as it's labelled as 'horror'. However I found there to be minimal 'puzzle' elements here, and any that did exist were fairly obvious to figure out. Instead the game is pushed forward by the other characters in the game, who clearly tell you what to do next at each stage.

So the focus of the game is mainly on the story, which I felt was pretty weak. The characters kept railroading me into doing things I didn't want to, like investigating a topic I didn't think had merit, or making me give information to somebody I didn't trust in order to push the plot forward. I thought the final reveal was bizarre and the 'villain's' motives were contrived. It seemed like the devs were trying to send some fancy message about society but hadn't done a good enough job of fleshing it out throughout the game so it all just felt flat at the end.

Several of the other reviews describe the tone of the plot as 'goofy', which I think is fitting but weird for a so-called horror game. Unfortunately the horror aspects solely comes from the occasional jump scare where an image pop ups with a scream, like the prank videos people used to send each other....

And lastly, there are 4 different endings, but getting them is really unsatisfying. To get the best ending, you have to constantly lie to people even if there is seemingly no reason to do so. The middle endings rely on you going out of your way to befriend a random stranger during a potential kidnapping, despite the game giving you many reasons to suspect them. Most people will choose to remain suspicious of every potential suspect but still not lie to anyone, and get the bad ending which makes all your work a waste of time.

review_text_raw:
I watched a playthrough of this game back in 2018, and I remember really liking it back then! When I was reminded of it's existence and heard positive buzz around it, I decided to try my hand at it. It is rather dated in some ways - the inclusion of a Twitter parody app, for one, and even the way characters post on that app scream early 2010's, and the other ways it's aged are just simply Millenialcore humor throughout - it also has quite a few typos (some more distracting than others), some of the voice acting is rough ("fuuuuuck thiiis sooooo muuuuuch" is now a repeated reference in my friend group for the absolutely baffling delivery lol). The plot and gimmicks are also rather predictable if you're at all familiar with this sub genre of horror media and akin sub genres. I recall the plot beats and phone gimmick/framing device being somewhat novel back in 2018, but maybe I misremember.

All that being said, I do enjoy this game and I think it's still worth playing! Some of my favorite things about this game are the soundscape (particularly the knocking and breathing noises randomly interspersed throughout), the interactivity and surprisingly accurate app design/aesthetics for some of the apps also helped immerse me, and I found myself very endeared to Anna and Ashley. This game is no masterpiece, but it's alright for what it is. I'd recommend you play it with a couple friends on voice call - y'all will have a good time leaving nonsense comments on the Jabbr posts, bullying Greg, being irked by Taylor, and making a bizarre dating profile!

The voice acting is terrible and feels very performative, rather than being believable phone calls/voice messages. The story is linear, and there isn't much room for creativity (e.g. sending people random pictures to see how they respond), and there aren't really any things to mess around with on the phone that are interesting. The puzzles are ridiculously simple and serve no purpose other than to slow down the narrative. The jump scares, if you consider them that, are pretty pointless and don't enhance the story or experience whatsoever. The writing is generally bad and unbelievable (e.g. [spoiler]the CEO of Phresh Ideas divulging way too much information [/spoiler]), and many of the dialog options do not make sense at all. The characters frequently go between texting and calling in a way that doesn't feel believable, and behave very strangely (e.g. [spoiler]at the end of the game, a character is literally texting you as he's pushing someone to their death off of a balcony [/spoiler]). After finishing the game you can go back through more quickly to see the alternate endings, but it still takes too long, and you still have to sit through a lot of dialogue at the end at the normal speed.

Ultimately I would not recommend purchasing this game, solely because the primary focus of this game is the narrative and it felt weak. I received this game from a bundle.

review_text_raw:
The story was nothing if not cliché. The concept of a found phone game is cool, or perhaps was at the time of release, but everything else surrounding this concept left me quite underwhelmed.

So many of the characters are creeps, and I find out I got the bad ending for not helping out either of the creeps continue their creep life.

Of course this isn't entirely true; there are mutliple endings. This was my first "found phone" type of mystery/horror to play so I was quite intrigued by the concept and mechanics as a whole. It really challenged how well of a snoop you were sometimes. Hilariously, I kept getting all the bad choices that ultimately led me to getting probably the worst ending possible and I wasn't really upset by that. However, there were some aspects that were a bit troubling for me throughout my playthrough. 

The jumpscares were considerably louder than the rest of the game and there are no audio options available. I guess I could understand if that was intentional since the "investigation" periods are very quiet (aside from [spoiler]the random knocks which were genuinely terrifying because I thought they were happening IRL[/spoiler]), but I actually did have fun just snooping through/messing with Anna's phone and texting everyone, so the cheap jumpscares took me out of the game pretty often.

Also, the climax (and the ending as a whole) just didn't totally sit right with me for some reason. Maybe my focus was waning by that point, but with hardly enough exposition to help drive the antagonist's motives, it just felt very out of left field. (Okay, maybe if I hadn't gone into this game ≈99% blind and maybe had also known [spoiler]what a simulacrum was[/spoiler], I would've had a better idea of what I was getting myself into.) With all that being said, I was left feeling underwhelmed and unsatisfied.

At the end of the day, SIMULACRA was [b]just okay[/b]. It's already very cheap in price, but I recommend you buy it during a sale if you're really that interested. I have just a small shred of hope for improvement on the second game.

Not the worst but I am surprised at how highly rated this was.
I didn't find it overly scary beyond a few jump scares.  The most believable characters in the game are Anna and her friend, I enjoyed their realistic sideconversations more than most others in this game.  The other 2 main characters were overhammed to the point of ridiculousness which was very jarring altogether.
The game gears and mechanisms running under the phone UI were just a little bit too visible to be believable.  As I found certain conversations softlocked at random points until you hit some other arbitrary checkpoint which unlocked the rest of the thread.  Also some things were just not implemented well.  In what world is a job interview carried out over text?  And every phone call was completely one-sided which was so strange - I don't know why they didn't let you select responses like in the written conversations.
Speaking of dialogue, I didn't feel I had great freedom of choice in responding in conversations - I felt I was always fighting with what I was allowed to say.  And the ending fell rather flat, with a certain character taking a complete 180 degree change in attitude and outlook just so the ending could be tied off in a semi-neat bow.
I do have the second game in the series as I got it in a bundle, and the game wasn't so awful as to put me off trying it, so I will see if these devs have taken on board lessons learned and improved things in the second go round, but this game as it stands I would not recommend it.

review_text_raw: This game had a slate of good ideas executed poorly. There are a ton of grammar mistakes in the English version that make situations unclear, and make the actions of characters within the story seem unrealistic, or come out of nowhere. The writing seems to come from a very immature perspective that seems to commodify women as sex objects. A lot of the game seems to want you to comply with the demands of the male characters, while the sole female character that knew the victim is uncooperative and aggressive toward you. The game chastised me for failing to get a guy to trust me, because he lied about having information I needed and wanted me to send him a picture of the victim from her phone in exchange for said information he didn't have. And even though I told him that was creepy and he seemed to understand, he later blew up at me for it and got himself killed. There's no sense of accountability, consistency, or predictability in these incredibly unrealistic interactions, and if it weren't for the lacking in that area of writing (and the sometimes horrible voice acting -- I'm looking at you, Greg), this could have actually been a very compelling and immersive game. Instead, the lack of payoff and random interactions render it a complete waste of time.
